speaker: Unknown
en: I think we can get started.
zh: 我想我们可以开始了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, everyone.
zh: 大家好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Gerry, co-founder and CEO of LlamaIndex, and today I'm excited to give a talk called Building the Document Context Layer for AI Agents.
zh: 我是 Gerry,LlamaIndex 的联合创始人兼 CEO,今天我很高兴做一个题为《为 AI 智能体构建文档上下文层》的演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really a big shout-out to the AI Engineer World Fair for hosting, and if you've seen some of my earlier talks from the previous AI Engineer conferences, we've kind of traced through a lot of the evolution of how, you know, agent advances have correlated with, you know, how you inject context into evolving applications.
zh: 非常感谢 AI Engineer World Fair 的主办,如果你看过我在之前几届 AI Engineer 大会上的一些早期演讲,我们其实一路追踪了很多演进历程,就是智能体的进步如何与——你知道的——如何向不断演进的应用中注入上下文相关联。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so today, in 2026, we'll kind of talk about three main topics.
zh: 那么今天,在 2026 年,我们会讲三个主要话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is, you know, what is RAG in 2026?
zh: 第一个是,你知道的,2026 年的 RAG 是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Two, that basically decomposes into an agent harness plus a context layer.
zh: 第二,它基本上分解为一个智能体 harness 加上一个上下文层。

speaker: Unknown
en: So kind of going into the modern document context layer for agents and giving you a little bit of sense of kind of some of the core capabilities today, especially unlocking, you know, the vast trove of document-based data today and give you a glimpse of what's next.
zh: 所以我们要深入讲一下面向智能体的现代文档上下文层,给你一点关于今天一些核心能力的感觉,尤其是解锁——你知道的——如今海量基于文档的数据,并给你一瞥接下来会是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right, RAG in 2026.
zh: 好的,2026 年的 RAG。

speaker: Unknown
en: But before that, just a little bit about the company, and I'll kind of get on with the main talk.
zh: 但在那之前,先简单讲一点关于公司的情况,然后我就进入正题。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might have seen us as a RAG framework.
zh: 你们可能见过我们,作为一个 RAG 框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started in 2023, got pretty popular, kind of create a lot of techniques around like advanced RAG, that type of stuff.
zh: 我们始于 2023 年,相当受欢迎,创造了很多技术,比如 advanced RAG 之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, we're basically the main document infrastructure for AI agents.
zh: 如今,我们基本上是 AI 智能体的主要文档基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: We deliver the best platform for agents to actually read and operate over documents, and we see ourselves as unlocking basically the vast troves of document context, even as agents and models themselves get better.
zh: 我们为智能体提供最好的平台,让它们真正读取并操作文档,我们把自己视为在解锁海量的文档上下文宝库,即使智能体和模型本身变得越来越好。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right, so what does RAG actually mean in 2026, and how are agents actually inhaling and adjusting context today?
zh: 好,那么 RAG 在 2026 年到底意味着什么,智能体如今实际上是如何摄入和调整上下文的?

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a snapshot from actually three years ago when I first gave a talk on this, and naive RAG was basically just building a simple chatbot over your private corpus of data.
zh: 这是三年前我第一次做这个演讲时的快照,naive RAG 基本上就是在你的私有数据语料上构建一个简单的聊天机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you flashback all the way to January of 2023, this technique basically consisted of you have some corpus of documents,
zh: 如果你回溯到 2023 年 1 月,这项技术基本上就是:你有一些文档语料,

speaker: Unknown
en: You chunk it up, embed it, and put it into a vector database.
zh: 你把它切块、嵌入,放进一个向量数据库。

speaker: Unknown
en: You do some naive top-k retrieval, and then you generate some stuff with an LLM.
zh: 你做一些 naive 的 top-k 检索,然后用一个 LLM 生成一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the steps are fixed.
zh: 所有步骤都是固定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You use kind of like a fixed set of techniques, and then with that, you actually get some basic application results by just being able to chat over a corpus of documents.
zh: 你使用一套固定的技术,然后凭借这个,你就能得到一些基础的应用结果,只是能够在一个文档语料上进行聊天。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, the agent landscape has changed quite a bit and quite dramatically since then.
zh: 当然,从那以后智能体的格局已经发生了相当大、相当剧烈的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is agent loops and tool use have gotten a lot, a lot better, especially as both the models and agent harnesses have increased.
zh: 一是智能体循环和工具使用已经变得好了很多很多,尤其是随着模型和智能体 harness 都在提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's basically a cleaner separation now between agent reasoning and how they actually interact with context.
zh: 而且现在智能体推理和它们实际与上下文交互的方式之间,基本上有了更清晰的分离。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at what I call kind of the modern generalized agent, which includes, you know, all your favorite applications and tools out there from Claude Code, Claude Cowork, OpenClaw, Codex, and a few others, you know, the retrieval complexity has started to get baked into the agent layer.
zh: 如果你看我称之为现代广义智能体的东西,它包括,你知道的,所有你喜爱的应用和工具,像 Claude Code、Claude Cowork、OpenClaw、Codex 等等,你会发现检索的复杂性已经开始被内置到智能体层中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So instead of coming up with a variety of hacks to really work around the limitations of naive top-k retrieval,
zh: 所以与其想出各种 hack 来绕过 naive top-k 检索的局限,

speaker: Unknown
en: You can start getting the agent to really reason about, for instance, the best keyword to search for, best search term to actually get back good results.
zh: 你可以开始让智能体真正推理,比如说,最好的搜索关键词是什么,最好的搜索词是什么,以真正拿回好的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if the retrieval tools are basic, the agent can input the right queries to basically loop upon itself and help solve the task at hand.
zh: 即使检索工具是基础的,智能体也可以输入正确的查询,基本上进行自我循环,帮助解决手头的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Number two, context is moving up the stack.
zh: 第二,上下文正在向栈的上层移动。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's been a lot of conversations, I think, for the first two and a half years of GenAI of how do you actually manage the agent context window, make sure it doesn't overflow, that type of thing.
zh: 在 GenAI 的前两年半里,有很多关于如何实际管理智能体上下文窗口、确保它不溢出之类的讨论。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think as, you know, a lot of the evolving techniques, compaction, long context have evolved, I think more and more of the conversation is actually how do you just hook up the right MCP servers and skills and tasks to the agent to enable it to do various types of tasks.
zh: 但我认为,随着很多不断演进的技术,compaction、长上下文的演进,我认为越来越多的讨论实际上变成了如何把正确的 MCP 服务器、技能和任务接入智能体,使它能够执行各种类型的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that also applies to agent orchestration, right?
zh: 所以这也适用于智能体编排,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Coding agents have gotten better.
zh: 编码智能体已经变得更好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Abstractions of actually defining what types of tasks and programs you want to build have moved a little bit upwards towards English as opposed to through code.
zh: 实际定义你想要构建什么类型的任务和程序的抽象,已经稍微向上移动,朝向英语,而不是通过代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so maybe in 2023 to 2025, you define programs and you still build stuff via like importing Python, using TypeScript through code.
zh: 所以也许在 2023 到 2025 年,你定义程序,你仍然通过像导入 Python、使用 TypeScript 通过代码来构建东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's pretty clear these days more and more people are just building stuff using English, whether you're a software engineer or you're in a non-technical function like go-to-market, marketing, and you're defining runbooks through English and kind of like defining the right goals and making sure that AI is aligned on the right task.
zh: 如今很清楚的是,越来越多的人只是用英语来构建东西,无论你是软件工程师,还是你在像 go-to-market、市场营销这样的非技术职能中,你通过英语定义 runbook,并且定义正确的目标,确保 AI 对齐在正确的任务上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we see that carrying over going forward as well.
zh: 我们看到这一点在未来也会延续下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in terms of just like general evolving knowledge work patterns, and this kind of forms a foundation for how we think about the context layer, you know, in the past maybe you could use AI to just like ask simple questions, get it resolved.
zh: 所以就一般演进的知识工作模式而言,这形成了我们思考上下文层的基础,你知道的,过去你也许可以用 AI 只是问一些简单的问题,把它解决掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today you're starting to be able to define and solve more end-to-end like tasks just through English and also use English to start compiling repeatable programs to actually execute something at scale.
zh: 今天你开始能够仅仅通过英语来定义和解决更多端到端的任务,并且还用英语开始编译可重复的程序,以实际大规模执行某些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, there's been a lot of discussion on how this will evolve even more, and we do see AI agents as behaving even more autonomously through solving long-horizon tasks, looping upon themselves to be able to achieve a goal.
zh: 显然,关于这将如何进一步演进,已经有很多讨论,我们确实看到 AI 智能体表现得更加自主,通过解决长时程任务,进行自我循环以能够达成一个目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the future will move towards a state where you actually might not even have to define the task in English, but actually more the goal and a scoring rubric, and then the agent will use all available contexts available to it to actually solve the task.
zh: 所以未来将走向一种状态:你实际上可能甚至不必用英语定义任务,而是更多定义目标和评分标准,然后智能体会使用它所有可用的上下文来真正解决任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with that overall framing, let's talk about what kind of is a pretty core focus for us as a company, which is basically helping to unlock unstructured context to basically feed into these agents even as they get really, really good, both in terms of the core model capabilities as well as the agent harness.
zh: 有了这个整体框架,让我们谈谈作为一家公司我们的一个相当核心的关注点,基本上就是帮助解锁非结构化上下文,以喂给这些智能体,即使它们变得真的、真的很好,无论是在核心模型能力方面,还是在智能体 harness 方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we'll focus a lot on our core focus area, which is document context, but of course there's plenty of other sources of context as well.
zh: 我们会大量聚焦于我们的核心关注领域,也就是文档上下文,但当然还有很多其他的上下文来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, we do think context really is everything.
zh: 事实上,我们确实认为上下文真的就是一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the end, you could have an infinitely smart agent, but your ability to actually get value out of this infinitely smart agent that's able to do more and more stuff end to end is actually giving it the right things to do.
zh: 归根结底,你可以拥有一个无限聪明的智能体,但你从这个能够端到端做越来越多事情的无限聪明的智能体中真正获得价值的能力,实际上是给它正确的任务去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the right things to do include the actual task, the goal,
zh: 而正确的任务包括实际的任务、目标,

speaker: Unknown
en: But also access to the vast troves of organizational context available to it.
zh: 但也包括对它可用的海量组织上下文宝库的访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether that is web search, web context, whether that is connectors through tools and skills and MCP servers, whether it's connectors through Snowflake or Databricks warehouses, or for us, whether it's access to the vast trove, like the 90% of documents are stored within SharePoint, Box, Dropbox, S3, all the unstructured data that's locked up within document containers.
zh: 无论是网页搜索、网页上下文,无论是通过工具、技能和 MCP 服务器的连接器,无论是通过 Snowflake 或 Databricks 数据仓库的连接器,还是对我们来说,无论是对海量宝库的访问——比如 90% 的文档存储在 SharePoint、Box、Dropbox、S3 中,所有被锁在文档容器里的非结构化数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for us, you know, we care a lot about how do you actually build the right tools and unlock the right context here.
zh: 所以对我们来说,你知道的,我们非常关心如何在这里实际构建正确的工具并解锁正确的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: We see documents as universal containers for unstructured context.
zh: 我们把文档视为非结构化上下文的通用容器。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's over 10 trillion-plus pages of human-native knowledge locked up within PDFs, PowerPoints, Word documents, and Excel sheets.
zh: 有超过 10 万亿页以上的人类原生知识被锁在 PDF、PowerPoint、Word 文档和 Excel 表格中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the same time, agents are also starting to generate exponentially more data in terms of, you know, more agent-native formats in terms of Markdown and HTML.
zh: 与此同时，智能体也开始以指数级速度生成更多数据，也就是更多智能体原生的格式，比如 Markdown 和 HTML。

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, building an agent-native document platform contains three main pieces.
zh: 对我们来说，构建一个智能体原生文档平台包含三个主要部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: It contains the document parsing layer, actually digitalizing the vast troves of PDFs, PowerPoints, and Word documents into kind of accurate, token-efficient context and feeding it either markdown, metadata, and other forms to actually enable agents to do stuff over your documents.
zh: 它包含文档解析层，即真正把海量的 PDF、PowerPoint 和 Word 文档数字化为某种准确且节省 token 的上下文，并以 Markdown、元数据以及其他形式输入，从而真正让智能体能够在你的文档上执行操作。

speaker: Unknown
en: The next is actually what we call the semantic and storage layer, which is kind of like this concept of document management for humans and agents.
zh: 第二部分是我们所说的语义与存储层，这有点像是面向人类和智能体的文档管理概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead of humans opening up Microsoft Word using your file system or file storage, how do you create some sort of agent interface that actually captures, stores all your documents and enables agents to actually manage and operate over them in various ways?
zh: 与人类打开 Microsoft Word、使用你的文件系统或文件存储不同，你如何创建某种智能体接口，真正捕获、存储你的所有文档，并让智能体能够以各种方式实际管理和操作它们？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's still room for actually kind of repeatable document workflows at the agent layer that you can actually encode within this type of platform too.
zh: 然后在智能体层，实际上仍有空间去做某种可重复的文档工作流，你也可以把它们编码进这类平台中。

speaker: Unknown
en: If there is a repeatable workflow like invoice processing, KYC, or claims, instead of always offloading it to a generalized agent, how do you actually develop some sort of specialized workflow for it and really carefully tune cost and accuracy to make sure that you achieve your goal?
zh: 如果存在一个可重复的工作流，比如发票处理、KYC 或理赔，与其总是把它交给一个通用智能体，不如你如何实际为它开发某种专门的工作流，并真正仔细地调整成本和准确率，以确保你达成目标？

speaker: Unknown
en: So, when we talk about the concepts today, in terms of these three layers, we'll talk about this concept of document OCR, which is one of the core concepts of this track, to document extraction, document search, and document workflows.
zh: 所以，当我们今天谈论这些概念时，围绕这三个层次，我们会谈到文档 OCR 这个概念，它是本主题的核心概念之一，然后是文档提取、文档搜索和文档工作流。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's still a variety of topics, yet left unsolved, from agent-native document formats, document versioning,
zh: 仍然有各种各样尚未解决的主题，比如智能体原生文档格式、文档版本管理，

speaker: Unknown
en: Document editing, you know, hill climbing as a service, and just like a wide set of kind of remaining concepts to actually create a comprehensive piece of software where agents and humans can collaborate on documents and actually do work over them.
zh: 文档编辑，也就是「爬山作为服务」，以及一大堆剩余的概念，用来真正创建一个完整的软件，让智能体和人类能够在文档上协作并真正在其上开展工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we'll start with the first section and maybe start kind of with the document OCR piece.
zh: 所以我们将从第一部分开始，也许先从文档 OCR 这一块讲起。

speaker: Unknown
en: First off, you know, document OCR is hard.
zh: 首先，文档 OCR 是很难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of you might have seen a blog post that we put out a few months ago related to this topic.
zh: 你们中有些人可能看过我们几个月前发布的与此主题相关的一篇博客文章。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the reason this problem even exists is an agent cannot actually take the raw PDF file binary and make sense of it.
zh: 但这个问题之所以存在，是因为智能体实际上无法直接拿到原始的 PDF 文件二进制并理解它。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's because the way PDFs are actually stored as a format is it's rendered for display purposes and not really for machine consumption in an interpretable manner.
zh: 那是因为 PDF 作为一种格式的实际存储方式，是为显示目的而渲染的，并不是真正为了以可解释的方式供机器消费而设计的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're designed for printing.
zh: 它们是为打印而设计的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, basically, texts are represented as almost like individual glyphs with coordinates.
zh: 所以，基本上，文本几乎是以带坐标的单独字形来表示的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tables are not represented as tables.
zh: 表格并不是以表格的形式表示的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're represented as, like, typically line segments drawn with various types of borders and also text drawn as certain cell positions.
zh: 它们通常表示为用各种类型的边框绘制的线段，以及绘制在特定单元格位置上的文本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you're kind of an agent that's trying to make sense of this like document, you're gonna have a really hard time actually trying to reason about what character and what shapes like map to what.
zh: 所以如果你是一个试图理解这种文档的智能体，你会很难真正推理出哪个字符、哪个形状对应的是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the whole point of document OCR, you know, it's been around for like 20 plus years, is to really try to create some sort of digitalized while interpretable representation that's both interpretable to humans as well as AI agents.
zh: 所以文档 OCR 的全部意义所在——它已经存在 20 多年了——就是真正尝试创建某种数字化的、可解释的表示，既对人类可解释，也对 AI 智能体可解释。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, reading order itself, if you have a multi-column layout, there is no guarantee that the way it's represented in the PDF actually corresponds to the typical ways that humans would read it.
zh: 另外，阅读顺序本身，如果你有一个多栏布局，并不能保证它在 PDF 中的表示方式与人类通常的阅读方式相对应。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because again, it's basically just an arbitrary sequence of characters drawn with coordinate positions.
zh: 因为再强调一次，它基本上只是以坐标位置绘制的任意字符序列。

speaker: Unknown
en: Related to this, even Word doc parsing is hard.
zh: 与此相关，即使是 Word 文档解析也很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're a little bit more structured than PDFs, but they're in kind of like this custom bespoke XML format, and this applies to PowerPoints as well.
zh: 它们比 PDF 稍微结构化一些，但它们处于某种自定义的定制 XML 格式中，PowerPoint 也是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: It contains more structural information, but still there's a ton of like fluff.
zh: 它包含更多结构信息，但仍然有大量的冗余。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you don't actually need to ingest all the tags to actually have the agent make sense of the Word document.
zh: 比如，你实际上不需要摄取所有标签，就能让智能体理解 Word 文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: It still needs to infer a bunch of structure from it.
zh: 它仍然需要从中推断出大量结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: It needs like the right kind of, to lift the right metadata around like formatting, semantics, that type of stuff.
zh: 它需要以正确的方式提取关于格式、语义之类的正确元数据，诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: But also being able to ignore the tags and actually being able to render the document so that the agent can see the overall structure of the page.
zh: 但同时也要能够忽略这些标签，并真正能够渲染文档，让智能体看到页面的整体结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still a generally hard problem and there's a lot of uplift you can get by actually parsing it into a more interpretable format instead of just using the native OXML and feeding that to an agent.
zh: 这仍然是一个普遍困难的问题，通过把它实际解析成更可解释的格式，而不是直接使用原生 OXML 并把它喂给智能体，你可以获得很大的提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're familiar with document understanding, you know, it's been around for quite a bit of time.
zh: 如果你熟悉文档理解，你知道，它已经存在相当长一段时间了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of these, like, heuristic and pipeline-based approaches which focused on kind of more, I guess, like, human-driven handwritten techniques to analyze, like, kind of various pieces of text, group them into clusters and identify tables, paragraphs, and be able to kind of, like, generate some sort of output representation.
zh: 有很多这类基于启发式和流水线的方法，它们更多地聚焦于，我想说，人类驱动的手写技术，来分析各种文本片段，把它们聚类分组，识别表格、段落，并能够生成某种输出表示。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of basic techniques if you use open source libraries like PyPDF, PyBeePDF, and, of course, some of the more recent approaches basically use this type of approach.
zh: 如果你使用像 PyPDF、PyBeePDF 这样的开源库，很多基础技术，当然还有一些较新的方法，基本上都使用这类方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's also, of course, using a VLM to one shot a document into text.
zh: 当然，还有使用 VLM 把文档一次性转成文本。

speaker: Unknown
